title: Inscribed tags and jars of Tomb U-j, Abydos
summary: Tomb U-j, a large multi-chambered burial in Cemetery U at Umm el-Qa'ab, Abydos, held about 150 perforated bone and ivory tags carrying incised signs, plus jars with ink marks. German Archaeological Institute excavators under Günter Dreyer published them in 1998; they are among the earliest known Egyptian writing, shortly before the First Dynasty.

uncertainty.note: Range is the "circa 3320 to 3150 BCE" span given by History of Information (radiocarbon-based per Dreyer's team; not independently checked here); Piquette gives Naqada IIIA1, c. 3300 / 3100 BCE. Year 3320 BCE = -3319, 3150 BCE = -3149.

where.historical_name: Abydos, Umm el-Qa'ab necropolis, Upper Egypt (Predynastic Naqada III, before the unified Egyptian state)

importance.justification: Among the earliest securely dated Egyptian writing, bearing on the origin of the script and early kingship.

sources.title: Inscribed Labels (chapter 11.06), in Writing as Material Practice
sources.author: Kathryn E. Piquette

sources.title: The Earliest Known Egyptian Writing, Circa 3320 to 3150 BCE

reviewer_note: Dates conflict by about 200 years across sources (3320 vs 3300 vs 3100 BCE); no source opened here gives the radiocarbon calibration directly. Coordinates are the Umm el-Qa'ab necropolis, not the tomb itself.
